legend: There is an old tradition of keeping 4 boxes of candies in the house in Cyberland. The numbers of candies are special if their arithmetic mean, their median and their range are all equal. By definition, for a set {x1, x2, x3, x4} (x1 ≤ x2 ≤ x3 ≤ x4) arithmetic mean is ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/daeb25d0b520beaea095158d4851903f527ffafc.png), median is ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7655b731471163052bb5fbb4c5414c495a2ca2e2.png) and range is x4 - x1. The arithmetic mean and median are not necessary integer. It is well-known that if those three numbers are same, boxes will create a "debugging field" and codes in the field will have no bugs.
For example, 1, 1, 3, 3 is the example of 4 numbers meeting the condition because their mean, median and range are all equal to 2.

Jeff has 4 special boxes of candies. However, something bad has happened! Some of the boxes could have been lost and now there are only n (0 ≤ n ≤ 4) boxes remaining. The i-th remaining box contains ai candies.
Now Jeff wants to know: is there a possible way to find the number of candies of the 4 - n missing boxes, meeting the condition above (the mean, median and range are equal)?
input: The first line of input contains an only integer n (0 ≤ n ≤ 4).
The next n lines contain integers ai, denoting the number of candies in the i-th box (1 ≤ ai ≤ 500).
output: In the first output line, print "YES" if a solution exists, or print "NO" if there is no solution.
If a solution exists, you should output 4 - n more lines, each line containing an integer b, denoting the number of candies in a missing box.

All your numbers b must satisfy inequality 1 ≤ b ≤ 106. It is guaranteed that if there exists a positive integer solution, you can always find such b's meeting the condition. If there are multiple answers, you are allowed to print any of them.
Given numbers ai may follow in any order in the input, not necessary in non-decreasing.
ai may have stood at any positions in the original set, not necessary on lowest n first positions.
note: For the first sample, the numbers of candies in 4 boxes can be 1, 1, 3, 3. The arithmetic mean, the median and the range of them are all 2.
For the second sample, it's impossible to find the missing number of candies.
In the third example no box has been lost and numbers satisfy the condition.
You may output b in any order.

output.ai: 如果存在解，在输出的第一行打印“YES”；如果不存在解，则打印“NO”。
如果存在解，你应该再输出 4 - n 行，每行包含一个整数 b，表示某个缺失盒子中的糖果数量。
你的所有数字 b 必须满足不等式 1 ≤ b ≤ 10^6。保证如果存在正整数解，你总能找到满足条件的这样的 b。如果有多组答案，你可以输出其中任意一组。
给定的数 ai 在输入中可能以任意顺序出现，不一定是非递减的。
ai 在原集合中可能位于任意位置，不一定在前 n 个最小的位置上。

note.ai: 对于第一个样例，4 个盒子中的糖果数量可以是 1, 1, 3, 3。它们的算术平均数、中位数和极差都为 2。
对于第二个样例，不可能找到缺失的糖果数量。
在第三个样例中，没有盒子丢失，并且数字满足条件。
你可以以任意顺序输出 b。

legend.ai: Cyberland 有一个古老的传统：在家中存放 4 盒糖果。如果糖果数量的算术平均数、中位数和极差都相等，那么这些糖果数量就是特殊的。根据定义，对于集合 {x1, x2, x3, x4}(x1 ≤ x2 ≤ x3 ≤ x4)，算术平均数为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/daeb25d0b520beaea095158d4851903f527ffafc.png)，中位数为 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7655b731471163052bb5fbb4c5414c495a2ca2e2.png)，极差为 x4 - x1。算术平均数和中位数不一定是整数。众所周知，如果这三个数相同，这些盒子就会产生一个“调试场”，场中的代码将不会有任何错误。
例如，1、1、3、3 是满足条件的 4 个数的一个例子，因为它们的平均数、中位数和极差都等于 2。
Jeff 有 4 个装有糖果的特殊盒子。然而，发生了一件糟糕的事情！其中一些盒子可能丢失了，现在只剩下 n（0 ≤ n ≤ 4）个盒子。第 i 个剩余的盒子中有 ai 颗糖果。
现在 Jeff 想知道：是否存在一种方案，确定丢失的 4 − n 个盒子中的糖果数量，并满足上述条件（平均数、中位数和极差相等）？

input.ai: 输入的第一行包含一个整数 n（0 ≤ n ≤ 4）。
接下来的 n 行每行包含一个整数 ai，表示第 i 个盒子中糖果的数量（1 ≤ ai ≤ 500）。
